visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. The KB-era index.html that used to sit in this directory was DELETED 2026-08-27: it was retired as a visual target on 2026-08-26 and kept only because ci:mockup-coverage required a parity.json beside any index.html, which is a gate keeping a dead file alive. The target is the patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE STILL BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow / Redfin / Windermere geo market pages. The answer in the first viewport (verdict, live figures, one source trace, one stamp, the monthly median series as Instrument.chart), sibling cities as Ledger doors, FAQ from the same buildMarketFaq array as FAQPage JSON-LD, and a single on-page ask.
note: Migrated off the dual KB/legacy register onto the v3 barrel 2026-08-13 (E-MARKET-REST). Both branches share V3Footer outside main. Rhythm: Breadcrumb, Instrument level 1 (chart on the Instrument, D9), Ledger (sibling cities), Quiet (FAQ), Sheet (inquiry), Quiet (edges), Footer. City chart is the newest-three-year monthly overlay from buildYearSeries, falling back to one chronological monthly line. Community chart is the 12-month median sale series when six or more complete months exist. Do not flatten those series to a figure. YTD / this-month / 12-month closed medians are Instrument figures, not a tabbed KB island. The verdict classifies the RAW months-of-supply value through marketVerdict(); formatMonthsOfSupply is display only. FAQPage JSON-LD moved from FAQBlock includeJsonLd onto MetadataBlock. Capture contract unchanged: GeoInquirySheet calls submitMarketPageInquiry with variant inquiry and fields name / email / message. KB-era deletions, city: KbHero, KbExploreTowns, KbArticles, FAQBlock, LeadCaptureBlock, KbSell, KbFooter, SmoothScrollProvider, MarketSources, KbMarketHud, KbMarketChart, KbTimeframeStats. Community deletions: PageBreadcrumb, HeroBlock, MarketSnapshot, MarketDetailStats, PriceBandTable stub, CityComparisonTable, ContentSection, FAQBlock, LeadCaptureBlock, RelatedAreas, CTABar, SiteFooter, DisplayHeading, buildNarrative, PriceChart. Closed-sales fields from the monthly cache row surface as Instrument figures on the community branch. marketHealthLabel is not printed.

tasteReview.beats: Redfin's Bend housing market page and Zillow's Bend home values page: this page wins on one clear sourced verdict with a two-bar months-of-supply trace and an honest 'as of' stamp. It loses on depth and breadth (no neighborhood breakdown, no inventory trend) and on motion.

defects.finding: The pager has the right shape: claim headline, prev/next, scrubbable line. But the digit-box tiles ($|7|5|9|K with shaded cells) read as a gimmick and look like a cream box. The pager has no scrubber rail or paged cards like the beautifului insight demo, so there is no visible way to see pages 2 and 3. It also needs an on-chart tooltip, not only text that says 'drag'.

The months-of-supply bars are correct, two named bars as the layout lock requires. But the card sits in a right column that is empty below it on desktop, so the first screen is lopsided. On mobile it pushes the headline claim above the pager. The 'As of Oct 3' and 'Oct 4' dates also disagree across the page.

defects.section: long-view median sale price chart and 'see the numbers' table
defects.finding: The 3-year chart is good, with hover tooltip, legend and navy/grey lines, but it is the same line chart repeated three times (insight 1, insight 2 and this one). The table below is a 36-cell scrolling list with no mark. Replace the cell text with in-cell bars or a heat strip, or fold it behind the chart's tooltip.

Counts such as 199 and $759K use a monospace digit-box animation. It is a decorative flourish, not a rolling number, and the boxed digits have uneven glyph spacing ('7 5 9'). Use a true number-swap with tabular numerals, and animate only live sourced figures.

defects.section: Bend at a glance + For sale now
defects.finding: A grey-on-cream prose paragraph with bold figures followed by a plain listing list. The prose repeats numbers already shown above, and the grey body text is low contrast. The listing rows have no map, no days on market and no price-change context, so there is no reason to scroll.

The fixed navy dog circle covers body text and table values at 375px (the Jul/Aug 2026 cells, the supply bars, glance paragraph). The chart legend labels also collide on mobile. Move the mascot into a corner dock that clears content and stack or truncate the legend.

The chart axis labels (Jan, Apr, Jun, Sep) are very light grey at roughly 10px, below AA contrast. Chart lines lack a y-axis in the first insight chart, so a reader cannot read values without hovering.

tasteReview.verdict: This is a correct, sourced, editorial page with a strong claim-first headline and a real months-of-supply bar pair. Past the first fold it settles into the same chart, a hairline table, a grey paragraph and a listing list, and the interaction is promised by text ('drag across the lines') more than shown. demoMatch is false: the insight pager is a custom text-and-chart panel without the catalog insight scrubber, and the digit tiles are not the number-swap demo. It is roughly a 77 page, a little under, because the mobile overlaps from the mascot and legend are real defects. I cannot confirm from these shots that SEO or listing information improved over HEAD, so both count as held, not improved, and that is itself a defect under this loop.
tasteReview.rebaselineReason: evaluatorModel grok-4.6 to claude-sonnet-5-5 (the chain's claude link now serves claude-sonnet-5-5) and shotsHash (the AEO change of 2026-10-04 adds the takeaways lead and the See the numbers table under every chart, and its states join the spec). Same-instrument check of the change itself, before and after on identical clips with one judge (cursor-grok-4.6-high, 2026-10-04): 50 -> 52, inside the rise floor of 3, so the look held. The mark this receipt is held to is the committed receipt's: 77. This scores 74 on the new instrument.
